pinning the write side in the same class as the read side wins over pinning one, because an implementation that never wrote would pass the other

refusing a named-line read that printed nothing wins over treating every empty output as a failure, which refuses the empty set
reading the unit the sentence states wins over changing the shape of flags(), which touches every row of the table

challenger_routes.why_considered: A goal of the form 'Write the text T to the file X and save the report to Y' returned status PASS__COMPOSED_CAPABILITY_CHAIN with pass=True after writing those 11 bytes into Y. X, the file the goal actually named, was never created on disk and the front door reported the goal done. Composition is attempted at exactly the two moments where the primary path has already failed, and both call sites returned the chain's own verdict untouched. The gate that catches this, promised_artifact_errors, had already run; its result was discarded.
challenger_routes.why_not_selected_or_selected: SELECTED: apply the gate that already exists to the fallback before it may report success. Two supporting defects were found by measuring the same family. (1) Template key order for the repair capabilities is output_path, source_root, test_argv, test_paths, and test_argv is derived FROM the test paths, so counting a derived argv as a competing claim cancelled the role against itself: exclusivity emptied a correct test_paths, the fallback then assigned every file in the sentence, source included. (2) That masking hid a second defect: _repo_paths only checks that a path RESOLVES under the root, so 'test command /usr/bin/python3 T' bound usr/bin/python3 as a test file and the adapter rejected it with FILE_INVALID. Both are fixed generally: an argv is not a claim, and a role list may only name files that exist. Measured: the false PASS becomes FAIL_CLOSED__PROMISED_ARTIFACT_MISSING naming the exact missing file; test_paths on the route-admission sentence returns exactly the named test; test_paths on the strict-progress sentence returns exactly the named test with no interpreter. Repair-family end-to-end pass rate unchanged at 1 of 6, which is stated rather than hidden: the remaining cause is the deliberate no-write-authority boundary.

recursive_obs.why_selected_route_is_fastest_sufficient: One condition added to an existing write-back decision, one helper that composes an address with a transform the table already knows, and one shape added to an existing predicate.  The dominant alternative -- a pipeline or a two-step chain for the compound sentences -- loses on measurement because sed already does both halves in one script, so the pipeline would add a shell as the verified operand to solve a problem that did not exist.  The second alternative, deciding read-versus-write from the script, is what the code already did and is exactly what measured as destroying a file.
